title: Interactive Punnett Square Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Biology
description: Interactive MicroSim that animates mono- and dihybrid Punnett squares, tracks genotype/phenotype counts, and lets students compare observed ratios to Mendelian expectations.

learningObjectives: Apply Punnett squares to determine genotype and phenotype outcomes for monohybrid crosses.
Compare live genotype/phenotype ratios from dihybrid crosses to the expected 9:3:3:1 distribution.
Explain how changing parent genotypes or gene letters alters gamete headers and resulting offspring.
prerequisites: Understands dominant vs. recessive alleles and capital/lowercase notation
Has solved a basic Punnett square manually

keyQuestions: Which gametes appear on the headers for the parents you selected?
How do the running genotype counts compare to the theoretical ratio?
What happens to the recessive phenotype when both parents are heterozygous?
commonMisconceptions: Believing that all heterozygous crosses produce 50% dominant and 50% recessive offspring
Confusing genotype labels when gene letters change
Thinking that mixing two heterozygous traits automatically yields equal phenotype categories
assessmentOpportunities: Have learners pause the animation halfway and predict the final ratios.
Ask students to screenshot a completed grid and annotate which cells are recombinant phenotypes.
